items.title: Erratum to "Long-term treatment with esketamine nasal spray in patients with treatment resistant depression: Results from the ESCAPE-LTE study" [European Neuropsychopharmacology 107 (2026) 112801].

summaries.en:
An important correction has been issued for a major study on esketamine nasal spray, a ketamine-based treatment showing real promise for people with severe depression that hasn't responded to traditional antidepressants. The original research tracked patients over the long term, and this update ensures the findings are as accurate as possible—because when we're talking about treatments that could genuinely help people who've tried everything else, getting the details right matters.

This kind of careful science is exactly what's driving the psychedelics field forward right now. Researchers aren't just discovering that these compounds work; they're doing the meticulous work of understanding how, for whom, and what happens when people use them over months and years. Every correction, every follow-up study, every honest conversation about limitations builds the solid foundation we need to bring these treatments into wider use.
summaries.da:
En vigtig rettelse er blevet udsendt til et større studie om esketamin-næsespray, en ketamin-baseret behandling, der viser rigtig potentiale for mennesker med svær depression, som ikke reagerer på almindelige antidepressiva. Det oprindelige forskning fulgte patienter over længere tid, og denne opdatering sikrer, at findingene er så præcise som muligt—fordi når vi taler om behandlinger, der kunne hjælpe mennesker, som har prøvet alt andet, betyder detaljerne virkelig noget.

Dette slag omhyggeligt videnskab er præcis det, der driver psykedelika-forskningen fremad lige nu. Forskere handler ikke bare om at opdage, at disse stoffer virker; de udfører det omhyggelige arbejde med at forstå hvordan, for hvem, og hvad der sker, når mennesker bruger dem over måneder og år. Hver rettelse, hver opfølgningsstudie, hver ærlig samtale om begrænsninger bygger det solide fundament, vi har brug for for at få disse behandlinger i bredere brug.

items.title: Psilocybin enhances sociability only in altered behavioural state and does not need an awake experience to be effective

summaries.en:
What if a psychedelic could help people with autism without the trip? New research suggests psilocybin can boost social behaviour in mice with autism-like traits—and here's the wild part: the effect works even when the brain is anaesthetised, meaning you don't need the hallucinations or altered consciousness to get the benefit. This challenges everything we thought we knew about how psychedelics work therapeutically.

Scientists gave psilocybin to mice genetically engineered to model autism spectrum disorder and saw lasting improvements in social interaction. The breakthrough came when they tested it under anaesthesia and found the same results. This opens a fascinating door: could we eventually create autism treatments based on psychedelics that deliver the healing without the mind-altering side effects? As psychedelic research moves from counterculture curiosity into legitimate medicine, studies like this help us understand which parts of the experience actually matter for healing.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis et psykedelikum kunne hjælpe mennesker med autisme uden at give et "trip"? Ny forskning tyder på, at psilocybin kan forbedre social adfærd hos mus med autisme-lignende træk—og her kommer det vilde: effekten virker selv når hjernen er bedøvet, hvilket betyder, at du ikke har brug for hallucinationer eller ændret bevidsthed for at få fordelen. Dette udfordrer alt, hvad vi troede, vi vidste om, hvordan psykedelika virker terapeutisk.

Forskerene gav psilocybin til mus, der var genetisk fremstillet til at modellere autismespektrumforstyrrelse, og så varige forbedringer i social interaktion. Gennembruddet kom, da de testede det under bedøvelse og fandt de samme resultater. Dette åbner en fascinerende dør: kunne vi engang udvikle autismebehandlinger baseret på psykedelika, der leverer helbredelsen uden de bevidsthedsforstyrrende bivirkninger? Når psykedelikaforskning bevæger sig fra modekulturfascination til legitim medicin, hjælper studier som dette os med at forstå, hvilke dele af oplevelsen som faktisk betyder noget for helbredelse.

items.title: Psychedelics in psychiatry: comparative effectiveness, implementation, commercialization and safety lessons learned from intranasal esketamine.

summaries.en: Esketamine—a nasal spray version of ketamine—is already helping people with severe depression in clinics across Europe and beyond. But here's what's really interesting: this real-world success story is teaching us crucial lessons about how to bring psychedelics safely and effectively into mainstream psychiatry. A new analysis looks at what esketamine's journey tells us about effectiveness, how to roll these treatments out properly, the business side of things, and most importantly, how to keep people safe. This matters because other psychedelics—like psilocybin and MDMA—are hot on its heels, and esketamine is essentially a test run showing us what works and what doesn't.
summaries.da: Esketamin—en næsespray-version af ketamin—hjælper allerede mennesker med alvorlig depression på klinikker rundt omkring i Europa og verden over. Men her er det virkelig interessante: denne succes i praksis lærer os afgørende lektioner om, hvordan man bringer psykedelika sikkert og effektivt ind i mainstream psykiatri. En ny analyse ser på, hvad esketamins rejse fortæller os om virkning, hvordan man udrullerer disse behandlinger ordentligt, forretningssiden af tingene, og vigtigst af alt, hvordan man holder mennesker sikre. Det betyder noget, fordi andre psykedelika—som psilocybin og MDMA—er lige bag efter, og esketamin er i princippet en testtur, der viser os hvad der fungerer og hvad der ikke gør.

items.title: Oncology Providers' Perspectives on Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy.

summaries.en:
Cancer doctors are getting questions about psychedelics—but most don't know how to answer. A new survey found that while nearly half of oncology providers have had patients ask about psychedelic-assisted therapy for end-of-life anxiety and depression, 80% don't feel confident counseling them. The main worry? Unknown interactions with cancer drugs and safety concerns. The good news: doctors who knew more about the emerging research were way more willing to explore it.

This study surveyed nearly 400 healthcare professionals across US cancer centers and palliative care networks. What it reveals is a critical gap—the science is moving forward, but the people actually treating patients haven't caught up yet. As psychedelic research for cancer-related suffering expands, closing this knowledge gap becomes essential. Education and access to trained treatment centers could be the missing piece that helps psychedelics reach the patients who need them most.
summaries.da:
Kræftlæger får spørgsmål om psykedelika—men de fleste ved ikke, hvordan de skal svare. En ny undersøgelse viser, at selvom næsten halvdelen af onkologiske læger har fået patienter, der spørger om psykedelika-assisteret terapi mod angst og depression ved livets slutning, føler 80% sig ikke trygge ved at vejlede dem. Hovedbekymringen? Ukendte interaktioner med kræftmedicin og sikkerhedsspørgsmål. Det gode nyhed: læger, der vidste mere om den nye forskning, var langt mere villige til at udforske det.

Denne undersøgelse omfattede næsten 400 sundhedsprofessionelle på amerikanske kræftcentre og palliativ behandling. Den afslører et kritisk tomrum—videnskaben skrider frem, men de mennesker, der faktisk behandler patienter, er ikke nået dertil endnu. Når forskningen i psykedelika mod kræftrelateret lidelse ekspanderer, bliver det afgørende at lukke dette videnshul. Uddannelse og adgang til erfarne behandlingscentre kunne være det manglende stykke, der hjælper psykedelika til de patienter, der har mest brug for det.

items.title: Development of Japanese Versions of the 4-Item Mystical Experience Questionnaire and 7-Item Challenging Experience Questionnaire.

summaries.en: When people take psychedelics in clinical settings, researchers need to measure what they actually experience — the profound, mystical moments and the challenging, difficult ones. Scientists have now created shorter Japanese versions of the key questionnaires used to capture these experiences, cutting down from 30 and 26 questions to just 4 and 7. This matters because it means faster assessments and less burden on participants, while keeping what makes these tools valuable. The study involved careful translation work guided by international standards, ensuring the questions feel natural and make sense for Japanese speakers. As psychedelic therapy edges closer to real-world use globally, having reliable measurement tools in different languages becomes essential — this is about making sure research can happen anywhere, and that the incredible experiences people have aren't lost in translation.
summaries.da: Når mennesker tager psykedelika i kliniske forsøg, skal forskere måle hvad de oplever — de dybe, mystiske øjeblikke og de udfordrende, vanskelige. Videnskabsfolk har nu skabt kortere japanske versioner af de vigtigste spørgeskemaer, der bruges til at indfange disse oplevelser, reduceret fra 30 og 26 spørgsmål til blot 4 og 7. Det betyder hurtigere vurderinger og mindre belastning på deltagerne, samtidig med at værktøjernes styrke bevares. Arbejdet involverede omhyggelig oversættelse ifølge internationale standarder, som sikrer at spørgsmålene føles naturlige for japansk-talende. Når psykedelisk terapi nærmer sig faktisk verdensomspændende brug, bliver pålidelige måleredskaber på forskellige sprog afgørende — det handler om at forskning kan ske overalt, og at de utrolige oplevelser mennesker har ikke går tabt i oversættelsen.

items.title: AMCP Market Insights: Optimizing managed care approaches to treatment-resistant depression.

summaries.en:
When standard antidepressants don't work—and for some people they simply don't—life can feel stuck. Treatment-resistant depression affects millions, draining quality of life and straining healthcare systems. Now psilocybin is emerging as a genuinely promising option for people who've tried everything else. A panel of healthcare leaders recently gathered to figure out how to actually make this work in practice: who should get it, how do we know it's worth the cost, and crucially, do we have enough trained therapists to guide people through the experience safely?

The study mapped out where psychedelic-assisted therapy fits into depression care right now—and it's clear the field is moving fast. Experts agree the evidence is real but want more data comparing psilocybin to other options and understanding exactly which patients benefit most. The biggest practical challenge? Building a real network of mental health professionals trained to administer and support these treatments. As psychedelics shift from research labs into actual healthcare systems, these questions matter enormously for patients waiting for hope.
summaries.da:
Når almindelige antidepressiva ikke virker—og for nogle mennesker gør de simpelthen ikke—kan livet føles låst fast. Behandlingsresistent depression rammer millioner og dræner livskvaliteten og belaster sundhedssystemet. Nu viser psilocybin sig som et ægte lovende alternativ for mennesker, der har prøvet alt. En gruppe sundhedsledere mødte for nylig for at finde ud af, hvordan man faktisk får det til at virke i praksis: hvem skal have det, hvordan ved vi, det er værd prisen, og afgørende—har vi nok uddannede terapeuter til at guide mennesker sikkert gennem oplevelsen?

Studiet kortlagde, hvor psykedelika-assisteret terapi passer ind i depressionsomsorg netop nu—og det er klart, at området udvikler sig hurtigt. Eksperter er enige om, at beviserne er reelle, men vil have mere data om at sammenligne psilocybin med andre muligheder og forstå præcis, hvilke patienter der profiterer mest. Den største praktiske udfordring? At opbygge et reelt netværk af psykiske sundhedsprofessionelle trænet til at administrere og støtte disse behandlinger. Når psykedelika skifter fra forskningstudier til egentlig sundhedspleje, betyder disse spørgsmål enormt for patienter, der venter på håb.

items.title: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy in Psychiatry: A Narrative Clinical Review of Mechanisms, Therapeutic Applications, and Emerging Evidence (2025-2026).

summaries.en:
Imagine a therapy where a single guided session with psilocybin could shift how your brain processes depression or trauma in ways that talk therapy alone might take months to achieve. New research is mapping exactly how this works—and it's pointing to something remarkable: psychedelics don't just mask symptoms, they seem to help your brain rewire itself. This clinical review brings together the latest evidence on how psilocybin-assisted therapy is being used in real psychiatric settings, showing concrete results for conditions that have resisted traditional treatment.

Researchers are synthesizing findings from clinical practice and studies to understand the mechanisms behind these effects. We're witnessing psychedelic research move from the margins into mainstream psychiatry, with mounting evidence that carefully guided experiences can catalyze genuine healing. This isn't hype—it's rigorous science catching up to something patients and therapists have been noticing: sometimes the most profound shifts come when we're brave enough to look inward with the right support.
summaries.da:
Forestil dig en terapi, hvor en enkelt guidet session med psilocybin kunne ændre, hvordan din hjerne behandler depression eller trauma—på måder, som samtale alene måske ville tage måneder at nå. Ny forskning kortlægger præcis, hvordan det virker—og det peger på noget bemærkelsesværdigt: psykedelika maskerer ikke bare symptomerne, de ser ud til at hjælpe din hjerne med at omstrukturere sig selv. Dette kliniske review samler den seneste evidens om, hvordan psilocybin-assisteret terapi bruges i rigtige psykiatriske behandlingssituationer og viser konkrete resultater for tilstande, som traditionel behandling hidtil har været machtesløs over for.

Forskere sammensætter fund fra klinisk praksis og studier for at forstå mekanismerne bag disse effekter. Vi er vidner til, at psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig fra periferien ind i mainstream-psykiatrien, med voksende evidens for, at omhyggeligt guidede oplevelser kan katalysere egentlig healing. Dette er ikke hype—det er stringent videnskab, som når ind til noget, patienterne og terapeuter har bemærket: nogle gange kommer de mest dybdegående skift, når vi er modige nok til at se indad med den rigtige støtte.

items.title: Efficacy and tolerability of ketamine in moderate to severe obsessive-compulsive disorder: a systematic review.

summaries.en: For the roughly half of OCD patients who don't respond to standard treatments, ketamine might offer a lifeline — but not in the way researchers initially hoped. A new systematic review found that a single ketamine infusion can spark rapid relief from obsessive thoughts in about half of patients, yet those benefits typically fade within a week. The real breakthrough? When ketamine was paired with therapy — specifically exposure and response prevention — patients experienced sustained improvement lasting weeks or months, suggesting the drug and therapy work together in ways we're still learning to understand. Researchers analyzed fifteen studies involving 118 participants using established review standards, uncovering both promise and caution: while ketamine proved safe overall, some patients experienced delayed mood crashes 24-48 hours after treatment. This finding adds crucial nuance to the psychedelics and mental health conversation — it's not about finding a magic molecule, but about using ketamine as a strategic tool alongside therapy to help people reclaim their lives from OCD.
summaries.da: For cirka halvdelen af OCD-patienter, som ikke responderer på standardbehandlinger, kan psykedelika som ketamin være et håb — men ikke helt som forskerne først håbede. En ny systematisk gennemgang viser, at en enkelt ketamininfusion kan skabe hurtig lindring fra tvangstanker hos cirka halvdelen af patienterne, men disse fordele forsvinder typisk inden for en uge. Det virkelige gennembrud? Da ketamin blev kombineret med terapi — specifikt eksponeringsterapi — oplevede patienter vedvarende forbedringer, der varede uger eller måneder, hvilket tyder på, at medicinen og terapien virker sammen på måder, vi stadig lærer at forstå. Forskerne analyserede femten studier med 128 deltagere efter etablerede standarder og afslørede både muligheder og forsigtighed: selvom ketamin viste sig sikkert generelt, oplevede nogle patienter forsinket stemningsfald 24-48 timer efter behandlingen. Denne opdagelse tilføjer vigtig nuance til samtalen om psykedelika og mental sundhed — det handler ikke om at finde et magisk molekyle, men om at bruge ketamin strategisk sammen med terapi.

items.title: Next-Generation Pharmacotherapies for Unipolar Mood Disorders: A Leading Article on Phase II/III Drug Development Across Diverse Mechanisms.

summaries.en: About one in three people with depression don't respond to standard antidepressants—and that's where things are finally getting interesting. A massive wave of new drugs is now in late-stage testing, tackling mood disorders through completely different biological pathways than the old approach. Psychedelics are part of this revolution, alongside cutting-edge compounds targeting glutamate, GABA, and ion channels. This review maps 24 promising drugs currently in Phase II/III clinical trials, showing how the field has exploded since FDA approval of esketamine and brexanolone opened the door to novel mechanisms. We're witnessing a genuine shift: after decades of similar treatments, science is finally offering real alternatives for people who've hit a wall with conventional therapy.
summaries.da: Omkring hver tredje person med depression reagerer ikke på almindelige antidepressiva—og det er netop her tingene bliver virkelig interessante. En massiv bølge af nye lægemidler er nu i sene testfaser og angriber depressioner gennem helt andre biologiske veje end den gamle tilgang. Psykedelika er en del af denne revolution, sammen med avancerede lægemidler der målretter glutamat, GABA og ionkanaler. Denne review kortlægger 24 lovende lægemidler i Phase II/III kliniske forsøg og viser hvordan området er eksploderet siden FDA godkendte esketamin og brexanolone og åbnede døren til nye mekanismer. Vi er vidne til et ægte skifte: efter årtier med lignende behandlinger tilbyder videnskaben endelig rigtige alternativer for mennesker, der har ramt en mur med konventionel terapi.

items.title: Psychedelic integration beyond the verbal: participatory-imaginal processing as a hypothesis-generating therapeutic framework.

summaries.en: What if the most healing parts of a psychedelic experience can't be put into words? New research suggests that when cancer patients take psilocybin, they often have intense, embodied experiences that simply don't translate into language—yet most therapy after the trip focuses on talking it through. Scientists now hypothesize that directly engaging with these non-verbal, imaginal experiences might actually be more powerful for lasting healing than trying to turn everything into a narrative. The team developed this idea by observing how psilocybin therapy actually works in practice, and it points to something bigger: we may need to rethink integration itself, moving beyond the talking cure toward approaches that honor the full spectrum of how psychedelics touch us.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis de mest helbredende dele af en psykedelisk oplevelse slet ikke kan sættes ord på? Ny forskning tyder på, at når kræftpatienter får psilocybin, oplever de ofte intense, kropsbundne erfaringer, som simpelthen ikke lader sig oversætte til sproget—alligevel fokuserer det meste terapi efter turen på at tale det igennem. Forskere har nu en hypotese om, at direkte arbejde med disse ikke-verbale, imaginative oplevelser måske faktisk er stærkere for varig helbredelse end at gøre alt til en historie. Teamet udviklede denne idé ved at observere, hvordan psykedelika-terapi virker i praksis, og det peger på noget større: vi må måske genoverveje integration selv, væk fra den talende kur mod tilgange, der værdsætter hele spektret af, hvordan psykedelika berører os.

items.title: Pilot study comparing the effects of high dose THC to high dose psilocybin and placebo in the set and setting of a classic psychedelic therapy session.

summaries.en:
Could THC be psychedelic? A tiny but fascinating new study says maybe—at least at high enough doses and in the right context. When four volunteers took 25mg of pure THC in a clinical setting designed for psychedelic therapy, their experiences looked strikingly similar to those on psilocybin. Some participants even thought they'd received a classic hallucinogen instead. This challenges what we thought we knew about cannabis and opens a curious question: does THC become genuinely psychedelic under specific conditions, or are we just seeing different sides of the same coin?

Researchers compared THC head-to-head with psilocybin and placebo in a controlled, double-blind study—the gold standard for this kind of work. It's early days with only four people, but it hints at something bigger happening in psychedelic science right now: we're realizing these substances might be far more nuanced and context-dependent than we assumed. As research expands beyond psilocybin and into adjacent territories, we're discovering that the psychedelic landscape is richer and stranger than the textbooks suggested.
summaries.da:
Kunne THC være psykedelik? Et nyt, lille studie rejser netop dette spørgsmål—og svaret er måske ja, i hvert fald ved høje doser og under de rigtige forhold. Når fire frivillige fik 25mg rent THC i en klinisk setting designet til psykedelisk terapi, lignede deres oplevelser slående meget dem fra psilocybin. Nogle deltagere troede endda, de havde fået et klassisk hallucinogen i stedet. Det udfordrer hvad vi troede vi vidste om cannabis og rejser et fascinerende spørgsmål: bliver THC virkelig psykedelisk under bestemte betingelser, eller ser vi bare forskellige sider af samme mønt?

Forskerne sammenlignede THC direkte med psilocybin og placebo i et kontrolleret, dobbeltkblind studie—det bedste vi har. Det er tidligt stadie med kun fire mennesker, men det peger på noget større i psykedelisk forskning lige nu: vi indser, at disse stoffer er meget mere nuancerede og kontekstafhængige end antaget. Når forskningen ekspanderer ud over psilocybin og ind i tilstødende territorier, opdager vi, at psykedelika-landskabet er rigere og mærkere end lærebøgerne fortalte os.

items.title: Salvinorin A in humans: A systematic review of pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety.

summaries.en: Salvia divinorum has been used in spiritual rituals for centuries, but we actually know very little about how it works in the human body—until now. A new systematic review reveals that salvinorin A, the plant's active compound, produces intense but short-lived psychedelic experiences and affects the brain differently than other psychedelics like psilocybin. Researchers analyzed existing studies to map out how the substance moves through your system, what it does to your brain, and what safety concerns exist. This deep dive matters because as psychedelic science expands beyond psilocybin and LSD, we need solid pharmacological data on lesser-known compounds. Understanding salvinorin A's unique profile could open doors to new therapeutic possibilities—or clarify why some traditional medicines work the way they do.
summaries.da: Salvia divinorum er brugt i spirituelle ritualer i århundreder, men vi ved faktisk meget lidt om, hvordan det virker i menneskets krop—indtil nu. En ny systematisk gennemgang afslører, at salvinorin A, plantens aktive stof, producerer intense men kortvarige psykedeliske oplevelser og påvirker hjernen anderledes end andre psykedelika som psilocybin. Forskere analyserede eksisterende studier for at kortlægge, hvordan stoffet bevæger sig gennem dit system, hvad det gør ved din hjerne, og hvilke sikkerhedsproblemer der eksisterer. Dette dybt dyk betyder noget, fordi når psykedelisk forskning udvider sig ud over psilocybin og LSD, har vi brug for solide farmakologiske data om mindre kendte stoffer. At forstå salvinorin A's unikke profil kunne åbne døre til nye terapeutiske muligheder—eller præcisere, hvorfor nogle traditionelle mediciner virker, som de gør.

items.title: As Psychedelic Treatments Get Leaner, Patients' Social Environments Deserve Attention.

summaries.en:
Here's something researchers are realizing as psychedelic therapy becomes more efficient: the people around you matter just as much as the medicine itself. A new study highlights that when we strip psychedelic treatments down to their essentials—fewer sessions, lower doses, streamlined protocols—we can't ignore what happens in patients' everyday lives. Your partner, your friends, your family, your support network—they're all part of the healing equation, whether we're paying attention to them or not.

This research comes at a pivotal moment in psychedelic science. As we're getting better at making treatments faster and more accessible, the field is waking up to something crucial: healing doesn't happen in a vacuum. The study reminds us that as protocols become leaner, we need to get smarter about understanding social context. It's a call for researchers and therapists to think bigger—not just about optimizing the medicine, but about optimizing the whole ecosystem around the person taking it.
summaries.da:
Her er noget, som forskere indser, når psykedelisk terapi bliver mere effektiv: de mennesker omkring dig betyder næsten lige så meget som medicinen selv. Et nyt studie fremhæver, at når vi gør psykedelisk behandling mere håndterlig—færre sessioner, lavere doser, strømlinede protokoller—kan vi ikke ignorere, hvad der sker i patienternes dagligdag. Din partner, dine venner, din familie, dit støtteapparat—de er alle del af helingsligningen, uanset om vi er opmærksomme på det eller ej.

Denne forskning kommer på et afgørende tidspunkt inden for psykedelisk videnskab. Mens vi bliver bedre til at gøre behandlinger hurtigere og mere tilgængelige, vågner feltet op til noget afgørende: helbredelse sker ikke i vakuum. Studiet minder os om, at når protokoller bliver mere effektive, skal vi blive smartere til at forstå social kontekst. Det er en opfordring til forskere og terapeuter om at tænke større—ikke bare om at optimere medicinen, men om at optimere hele økosystemet omkring den person, der tager den.

items.title: Case report of S-ketamine as treatment option for suicidal ideation and treatment-resistant depression in adolescents with early-onset psychosis.

summaries.en: A 16-year-old with schizophrenia and persistent suicidal thoughts found relief when doctors added S-ketamine to his treatment—his depression scores dropped by half in just three weeks, and his psychotic symptoms actually improved too. This is striking because ketamine is usually considered risky for people with psychosis, yet this teenager showed rapid recovery without any worsening of his condition. Researchers gave him intranasal S-ketamine after standard antipsychotics alone couldn't touch his depression. This case hints at something bigger: psychedelics and ketamine-like compounds are opening doors for treating severe depression that doesn't respond to conventional medicine, even in tricky situations like early-onset psychosis. It's early evidence, but it suggests we need more research into how these molecules might help young people in real crisis.
summaries.da: En 16-årig med skizofreni og vedvarende selvmordstanker fandt lindring, da lægerne tilføjede S-ketamin til hans behandling—hans depressionsscorer faldt med halvdelen på bare tre uger, og hans psykotiske symptomer blev faktisk bedre. Det er slående, fordi ketamin normalt betragtes som risikabelt for personer med psykose, men denne teenager viste hurtig bedring uden forværring af sin tilstand. Forskere gav ham næsespray med S-ketamin, efter at standard antipsykotika alene ikke kunne hjælpe hans depression. Denne case peger på noget større: psykedelika og ketaminklignende stoffer åbner døre for behandling af svær depression, der ikke reagerer på konventionel medicin, selv i tricky situationer som tidlig psykose. Det er tidlige tegn, men det foreslår, at vi har brug for mere forskning i, hvordan disse molekyler kunne hjælpe unge mennesker i real krise.

items.title: Beyond head-twitch response: Acute psilocybin affects spontaneous behaviors in rats in a dose-dependent manner.

summaries.en: Scientists just discovered that psilocybin does way more to the brain than we thought — it's not just about the famous head-twitch response. When rats received different doses of psilocybin, their entire behavioral repertoire shifted in fascinating ways: they moved less, stopped grooming themselves, and changed how they explored their environment, with each behavior responding to different dose levels. Researchers gave male and female rats varying amounts of psilocybin and carefully filmed what happened next, identifying seven distinct behavioral changes that paint a much richer picture of how the drug actually works in the brain. This matters because as psychedelics move toward real clinical use for depression, anxiety, and PTSD, understanding these detailed behavioral effects helps scientists decode exactly which brain systems are involved — and that knowledge could be the key to making treatments safer and more effective.
summaries.da: Forskere har lige opdaget, at psykedelika påvirker hjernen på langt flere måder end vi troede — det handler ikke bare om det berømte hovedrystelsessvar. Da rotter fik forskellige doser psilocybin, ændrede hele deres adfærdsmønster sig på fascinerende vis: de flyttede mindre, stoppede med at pudse sig, og ændrede hvordan de udforsker deres miljø, hvor hver adfærd reagerede på forskellige dosis-niveauer. Forskerne gav han- og hun-rotter varierende mængder psilocybin og filmede omhyggeligt hvad der skete bagefter, og identificerede syv forskellige adfærdsændringer, der tegner et meget rigere billede af hvordan stoffet rent faktisk virker i hjernen. Det betyder noget, fordi når psykedelika bevæger sig mod rigtig klinisk brug mod depression, angst og PTSD, hjælper forståelsen af disse detaljerede adfærdsvirkninger videnskabsfolk med at dekode præcis hvilke hjernebaner der er involveret — og den viden kunne være nøglen til at gøre behandlinger sikrere og mere effektive.

items.title: Exploring Ayahuasca Multitarget Potential in Neuropsychiatric Disorders: Integrated Insights Towards Drug Discovery

summaries.en: What if one plant medicine could hit multiple targets in the brain at once, instead of relying on single-drug fixes that often fall short? New research reveals that ayahuasca—a traditional Amazonian brew—interacts with a whole network of brain receptors and molecular pathways involved in depression, anxiety, trauma, and other neuropsychiatric conditions. Scientists used network pharmacology to map how ayahuasca's active compounds dance with dozens of brain targets simultaneously, uncovering a complex biological symphony that may explain why people report such profound healing experiences. This isn't hype: the study carefully traced the molecular fingerprints connecting ayahuasca to key genes and pathways known to matter in mental health. As psychiatry increasingly recognizes that one-size-fits-all drugs don't work for everyone, this research points to a bigger shift—toward understanding how plants and compounds that work on multiple targets might offer what single-target drugs cannot. It's early days, and ayahuasca's variable composition means we're not ready to prescribe it in clinics yet, but this work builds the scientific foundation for smarter, more holistic approaches to treating neuropsychiatric disorders.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis ét plantemedicinsk stof kunne påvirke flere målgrupper i hjernen samtidigt, i stedet for at stole på enkeltdosis-behandlinger, der ofte kommer til kort? Ny forskning viser, at ayahuasca—en traditionel amazonas-drik—interagerer med et helt netværk af hjernereceptorer og molekylære veje involveret i depression, angst, trauma og andre neuropsykiatriske tilstande. Forskere brugte netværkfarmakologi til at kortlægge, hvordan ayahuascas aktive stoffer danser sammen med duetvis af hjernens målpunkter samtidigt, og afslørede en kompleks biologisk symfoni, som måske forklarer, hvorfor mennesker rapporterer så dybtgående helbredelsesoplevelser. Dette er ikke hyper: studiet sporede omhyggeligt de molekylære fingeraftryk, der forbinder ayahuasca til vigtige gener og veje kendt for at betyde noget indenfor mental sundhed. Eftersom psykiatrien i stigende grad erkender, at enhedslösninger ikke virker for alle, peger denne forskning mod en større udvikling—mod at forstå, hvordan planter og stoffer, der påvirker flere målpunkter, kunne give det som enkeltmål-lægemidler ikke kan. Det er stadig tidligt, og ayahuascas varierende sammensætning betyder, vi ikke er klar til at ordinere det på klinikker endnu, men dette arbejde bygger det videnskabelige fundament for smartere, mere helstøbte tilgange til behandling af neuropsykiatriske lidelser.

items.title: AI-mediated relational competence and its limits: Psychedelic-assisted therapy as a stress case and policy signal

summaries.en:
What happens when AI tries to help therapists guide people through profound emotional experiences? A new study examines psychedelic-assisted therapy as a fascinating test case for AI's limits in human connection. The research reveals that while AI can handle certain therapeutic tasks, the deep relational work—the real listening, presence, and attunement that makes therapy transformative—still needs a human touch. This matters because psychedelics work by opening people up emotionally and cognitively in ways that demand genuine human understanding.

The study looked at how AI could support therapists in psychedelic sessions and found important boundaries. As psychedelic research advances and more people may access these treatments, this raises crucial questions: What roles can technology play without compromising the therapeutic relationship? The findings signal something bigger—that some of the most meaningful healing requires irreplaceably human skills, and that's worth protecting even as medicine becomes more high-tech.
summaries.da:
Hvad sker der, når AI skal hjælpe terapeuter med at guide mennesker gennem dybt følelsesmæssige oplevelser? Et nyt studie undersøger psykedelika-assisteret terapi som et fascinerende testcase for AIs grænser inden for menneskelig forbindelse. Forskningen viser, at selvom AI kan håndtere visse terapeutiske opgaver, kræver det dybe relationelle arbejde—det ægte lytning, nærvær og indlevelse, der gør terapi transformativ—stadig menneskeligt nærvær. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelika virker ved at åbne mennesker op følelsesmæssigt og kognitivt på måder, der kræver ægte menneskelig forståelse.

Studiet undersøgte, hvordan AI kunne støtte terapeuter i psykedelika-sessioner, og fandt vigtige grænser. Efterhånden som psykedelika-forskning skrider frem og flere mennesker kan få adgang til disse behandlinger, rejser det afgørende spørgsmål: Hvilke roller kan teknologi spille uden at kompromittere den terapeutiske relation? Resultaterne signalerer noget større—at noget af den mest meningsfulde helbredelse kræver uerstattelig menneskelig indsigt, og det er værd at værne om, selv når medicinen bliver mere højteknologisk.

items.title: The Strangest Drug Ever Studied: The Chemical Structure, History, and Enduring, Conjecturing Mystery of DMT

summaries.en:
DMT might be the strangest drug science has ever studied. People report encounters with entities, radical shifts in how they perceive reality, and experiences that feel more real than waking life—changes that can last long after the experience ends. Now researchers are using brain imaging to understand what's actually happening in the brain during these intense journeys, exploring how DMT might reshape our sense of self and consciousness itself.

This new paper traces DMT from Indigenous Amazonian traditions through a century of scientific fascination, prohibition, and today's clinical research renaissance. While we know DMT's chemical structure mirrors serotonin and occurs naturally in plants, mammals, and possibly our own bodies, its true biological purpose and how it creates such overwhelming experiences remain mysteries. As psychedelic science accelerates, DMT sits at the heart of big questions about consciousness—making it essential territory for anyone curious about what the human brain is truly capable of.
summaries.da:
DMT er måske det mærkeligste stof, videnskaben nogensinde har studeret. Folk rapporterer møder med væsener, radikale skift i deres opfattelse af virkeligheden og oplevelser, der føles mere reelle end vågent liv—ændringer der kan vare længe efter oplevelsen er forbi. Nu bruger forskere hjernescanning til at forstå, hvad der faktisk sker i hjernen under disse intense rejser, og udforsker hvordan psykedelika kan omforme vores selvopfattelse og bevidsthed.

Dette nye arbejde sporer psykedelika fra oprindelige amazonske traditioner gennem et århundrede af videnskabelig fascination, forbud og dagens kliniske forskningsrenaissance. Selvom vi kender psykedelikas kemiske struktur, der afspejler serotonin og forekommer naturligt i planter, pattedyr og muligvis vores egne kroppe, forbliver dets sande biologiske formål og hvordan det skaber så overvældende oplevelser mysterier. Mens psykedelisk forskning accelererer, sidder psykedelika i hjertet af store spørgsmål om bevidsthed—hvilket gør det vigtig område for alle, der er nysgerrige på, hvad den menneskelige hjerne virkelig er i stand til.

items.title: The Strangest Drug Ever Studied: The Chemical Structure, History, and Enduring, Conjecturing Mystery of DMT

summaries.en: DMT might be the strangest drug science has ever encountered. People describe it as launching them into radically alien worlds where they meet entities, experience mystical visions, and walk away fundamentally changed—all in minutes. What's wild is that this molecule isn't just something someone cooked up in a lab; it occurs naturally in plants used for centuries in Amazonian rituals, in mammals, and possibly even in your own brain. Researchers like Rick Strassman and Chris Timmermann are now using brain imaging to map what's happening during DMT experiences, discovering that it rewires how different brain regions communicate and seems to dissolve our everyday sense of self. The honest truth? We still don't fully understand how DMT works or why it exists in our bodies at all. But that mystery is exactly why psychedelics research is exploding right now—DMT sits at this fascinating crossroads where chemistry, consciousness, and neuroscience collide, and every new study edges us closer to understanding what it can teach us about the mind.
summaries.da: DMT kan være det mærkeligste stof, som videnskaben nogensinde har mødt. Mennesker beskriver, hvordan det katapulterer dem ind i radikalt fremmedartede verdener, hvor de møder væsner, oplever mystiske visioner og går derfra fundamentalt forandrede—alt på få minutter. Det bizarre er, at dette molekyle ikke bare er noget, nogen har skabt på et laboratorium; det optræder naturligt i planter, som er brugt i århundreder i amazonske ritualer, i pattedyr og muligvis endda i din egen hjerne. Forskere som Rick Strassman og Chris Timmermann bruger nu hjernescanning til at kortlægge, hvad der sker under psykedelika-oplevelser, og de opdager, at det omkonfigurerer, hvordan forskellige hjernedele kommunikerer, og ser ud til at opløse vores dagligdags fornemmelse af selvet. Den ærlige sandhed? Vi forstår stadig ikke helt, hvordan psykedelika virker, eller hvorfor det findes i vores kroppe. Men det er netop det mysterium, der får psykedelika-forskningen til at eksplodere lige nu—psykedelika sidder ved denne fascinerende krydsning af kemi, bevidsthed og neuroscience.

items.title: Adverse Effect-Related Language in Recreational Psychedelic and non-Psychedelic Substance Experience Reports

summaries.en:
What actually happens when people use psychedelics recreationally? Researchers analyzed thousands of online trip reports to find out, comparing experiences with LSD, psilocybin, DMT, ketamine, MDMA, and ayahuasca. The results are sobering in places: ayahuasca users reported the most vomiting, ketamine users experienced intense dissociation, and MDMA came with drowsiness and heart concerns. This matters because we rarely know what real-world adverse effects look like outside the lab.

Using artificial intelligence to read natural language patterns, scientists mapped these reports against known medical literature on side effects—a clever way to understand what recreational users actually experience. As psychedelic research accelerates toward clinical use, understanding what can go wrong in uncontrolled settings helps researchers and clinicians prepare better safety protocols and honest conversations with people considering these substances.
summaries.da:
Hvad sker der egentlig når mennesker bruger psykedelika rekreativt? Forskere analyserede tusindvis af online trip reports for at finde ud af det, og sammenlignede oplevelser med LSD, psilocybin, DMT, ketamin, MDMA og ayahuasca. Resultaterne er pletvis alvorlige: ayahuasca-brugere rapporterede mest kvalme, ketamin-brugere oplevede intens dissociation, og MDMA kom med søvnighed og hjertebetænkeligheder. Det betyder noget, fordi vi sjældent ved hvad virkelige bivirkninger ser ud som uden for laboratoriet.

Ved hjælp af kunstig intelligens til at læse naturligt sprog-mønstre kortlagde videnskabsmænd disse rapporter mod kendt medicinsk litteratur om bivirkninger—et smart trick til at forstå hvad faktiske brugere oplever. Når psykedelika-forskningen accelererer mod klinisk brug, hjælper forståelse af hvad der kan gå galt i ukontrollerede omgivelser forskere og klinikere med at forberede bedre sikkerhedsprotokoller og ærlighed over for mennesker der overvejer disse stoffer.

items.title: Psicodélicos no tratamento da depressão: evidências atuais e perspectivas futuras

summaries.en:
Depression that doesn't budge with standard antidepressants? New research suggests psychedelics like psilocybin might offer real hope. Studies show significant drops in depressive symptoms after psilocybin treatment—often faster than traditional medications—especially for people who've tried everything else. The effect seems strongest when psychedelics are paired with psychological support, suggesting the mind and medicine work together here.

This is a literature review analyzing current evidence on how psychedelics work in depression treatment, looking at effectiveness, safety, and how they compare to conventional approaches. What's exciting is that psychedelics are shifting from fringe idea to serious clinical contender, filling a genuine gap where traditional treatments fall short. We're watching the field move from "this might work" to "here's how and why"—and that's changing treatment possibilities for millions.
summaries.da:
Depression der ikke reagerer på almindelige antidepressiva? Ny forskning tyder på, at psykedelika som psilocybin kan give håb. Studier viser markant reduktion i depressive symptomer efter psilocybin-behandling—ofte hurtigere end traditionelle mediciner—især for mennesker, der har prøvet alt muligt. Effekten ser ud til at være stærkest, når psykedelika kombineres med psykologisk støtte, hvilket tyder på, at sind og medicin arbejder sammen.

Dette er en litteraturgennemgang, der analyserer nuværende evidens for, hvordan psykedelika virker ved depression, med fokus på effektivitet, sikkerhed og sammenligning med konventionelle tilgange. Det spændende er, at psykedelika bevæger sig fra randfænomen til seriøs klinisk mulighed og udfylder et ægte tomrum, hvor traditionelle behandlinger ikke virker. Vi ser feltet bevæge sig fra "det kunne virke" til "sådan virker det"—og det ændrer behandlingsmuligheder for millioner.

items.title: JAMA study examines Oregon's psilocybin services model

summaries.en: What happens when psychedelics leave the lab? Oregon just gave us the first real-world answer. A new JAMA study tracked people using psilocybin through the state's regulated program—and the early results are encouraging. Most people reported meaningful improvements in their mental health, with relatively few serious adverse events. This isn't a controlled clinical trial where everything is perfectly managed; it's actual people seeking help through an actual legal system. That distinction matters enormously, because it shows us what psychedelic-assisted therapy might actually look like when it becomes available to regular people. The research team examined real outcomes from Oregon's pioneering model, giving us crucial data on both benefits and risks outside the sterile conditions of a research lab. As psychedelics move from fringe curiosity toward mainstream medicine, this study is exactly the kind of evidence we need—proof that these therapies can work safely in the messy, complicated world most of us actually live in.
summaries.da: Hvad sker der, når psykedelika forlader laboratoriet? Oregon gav os netop det første virkeligt svar. Et nyt JAMA-studie fulgte mennesker, der brugte psilocybin gennem statens regulerede program—og de foreløbige resultater er lovende. De fleste rapporterede meningsfulde forbedringer i deres mentale helbred, med relativt få alvorlige bivirkninger. Dette er ikke et kontrolleret klinisk forsøg, hvor alt er perfekt styret; det er rigtige mennesker, der søger hjælp gennem et rigtigt juridisk system. Den forskel betyder enormt meget, fordi den viser os, hvordan psykedelika-assisteret terapi faktisk kunne se ud, når det bliver tilgængeligt for almindelige mennesker. Forskerholdet undersøgte virkelige resultater fra Oregons banebrydende model og gav os afgørende data om både fordele og risici uden for laboratoriets sterile forhold. Når psykedelika bevæger sig fra marginale nysgerrighed mod mainstream medicin, er dette studie præcis den form for evidens, vi har brug for—bevis på, at disse behandlinger kan fungere sikkert i den uordentlige, komplicerede verden, de fleste af os faktisk lever i.

items.title: Exploring Psychedelics as Novel Therapeutics for Smoking Cessation: Mechanistic Insights from Animal Studies

summaries.en:
What if the key to quitting smoking wasn't willpower alone, but a compound that could reset how your brain experiences addiction? New research shows psilocybin significantly reduced nicotine withdrawal symptoms and cravings in animal studies—and the effects were surprisingly broad, also helping with opioid dependence. This suggests psychedelics might work on addiction itself, not just individual drugs.

Scientists used mouse models to trace exactly what's happening in the brain: psilocybin appears to rewire the neural circuits that drive dependence, changing how genes related to addiction are expressed. As smoking remains a leading preventable cause of death worldwide and current treatments often fail, this research points toward a radically different approach—one that could eventually help millions of people break free from nicotine for good.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis nøglen til at stoppe med at ryge ikke kun handler om vilje, men om et stof der kunne nulstille, hvordan din hjerne oplever afhængighed? Ny forskning viser, at psilocybin signifikant reducerede nikotinabstinenser og trang efter nikotin hos dyr—og effekterne var overraskende brede og hjalp også med opioidafhængighed. Det tyder på, at psykedelika kunne påvirke selve afhængigheden, ikke blot enkelte stoffer.

Forsker brugte musemodeller til at spore præcis, hvad der sker i hjernen: psilocybin ser ud til at omstrukturere de nervecirkler, der driver afhængighed, og ændrer hvordan gener relateret til afhængighed udtrykt. Eftersom rygning fortsat er en ledende undgåelig dødsårsag verden over, og nuværende behandlinger ofte mislykkes, peger denne forskning mod en radikalt anderledes tilgang—en der kunne hjælpe millioner af mennesker ud af nikotinafhængighed for godt.

items.title: Combination of psychedelic, CBT shows promise in AUD treatment

summaries.en: Imagine feeling like you've been given a second chance. In a new study, people struggling with alcohol addiction described their experience with a single dose of psychedelics combined with talk therapy as transformative—using words like "cleansing" and "rebirth." The results? Eight out of ten participants cut back or stopped drinking altogether over the next three months. Researchers gave participants one psychedelic dose alongside cognitive-behavioral therapy in this early Phase 2a trial. This fits into a larger shift in addiction medicine: psychedelics aren't being studied as magic bullets, but as catalysts that help people engage more deeply with therapy and reimagine their relationship with substances. It's not easy—participants were honest about the challenges—but the promise is real.
summaries.da: Forestil dig at få en anden chance. I en ny undersøgelse beskrev mennesker, der kæmper med alkoholforgiftning, deres erfaring med en enkelt dosis psykedelika kombineret med terapi som transformativ—med ord som "renselse" og "genfødelse." Resultaterne? Otte ud af ti deltagere drak mindre eller holdt helt op i løbet af de næste tre måneder. Forskerne gav deltagerne én psykedelika-dosis sammen med kognitiv adfærdsterapi i dette tidlige fase 2a-forsøg. Det passer ind i en større bevægelse inden for afhængighedsmedicin: psykedelika bliver ikke studeret som vidundermidler, men som katalysatorer, der hjælper mennesker til at engagere sig dybere med terapi og omtænke deres forhold til stoffer. Det er ikke nemt—deltagerne var ærlige om udfordringerne—men løftet er reelt.

items.title: Ketamine Safety and Therapeutic Opportunity in Late-Life Depression With Depression-Executive Dysfunction Syndrome (DED).

summaries.en:
What if a single dose could lift depression in older adults within hours instead of weeks? New research is exploring ketamine's potential for treating late-life depression, especially in people who struggle with both low mood and executive function — the mental skills we need to plan, decide, and get things done. Early findings suggest ketamine might work differently than traditional antidepressants, offering hope for those who haven't responded to conventional treatments.

Scientists studied how ketamine affects this specific group, focusing on safety and effectiveness. This research slots into a bigger shift happening right now: psychedelics and related compounds like ketamine are being rigorously tested not as party drugs, but as precision tools for mental health. As our population ages and depression becomes increasingly resistant to standard care, understanding these alternative pathways could genuinely reshape how we treat suffering in older people.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis en enkelt dosis kunne løfte depression hos ældre voksne inden for timer i stedet for uger? Ny forskning udforsker ketamins potentiale til at behandle depression i høj alder, især hos mennesker, der kæmper med både dårligt humør og eksekutive funktioner — de mentale færdigheder, vi bruger til at planlægge, træffe beslutninger og få tingene gjort. Tidlige resultater tyder på, at ketamin kunne virke anderledes end traditionelle antidepressiva og give håb til dem, der ikke har reageret på konventionel behandling.

Forskerene undersøgte, hvordan ketamin påvirker denne særlige gruppe, med fokus på sikkerhed og effektivitet. Denne forskning passer ind i et større skifte, der sker netop nu: psykedelika og beslægtede stoffer som ketamin bliver grundigt testet — ikke som fester-stoffer, men som præcisions-værktøjer for mental sundhed. Efterhånden som vores befolkning bliver ældre og depression bliver stadigt mere modstandsdygtig over for standard behandling, kunne forståelsen af disse alternative veje faktisk omforme måden, vi behandler lidelse hos ældre mennesker på.

items.title: Depression Heterogeneity as a Confounder in Ketamine Response for Late-Life Depression.

summaries.en: Not everyone responds to ketamine the same way—and that might be the whole point. New research suggests that depression in older adults isn't one condition but many, and ketamine's effects depend heavily on which type you actually have. This matters because it could explain why some people experience dramatic relief while others see little change, and it hints that we might need to get much better at matching the right treatment to the right person. The study examined how depression varies in late-life patients and how this variation shapes ketamine's effectiveness. As psychedelics research accelerates, this finding points to a crucial frontier: moving beyond one-size-fits-all medicine toward precision treatments tailored to individual biology and psychology. Understanding these differences isn't just academic—it's the key to unlocking psychedelics' real potential in the clinic.
summaries.da: Ikke alle reagerer ens på ketamin—og det kan være hele pointen. Ny forskning tyder på, at depression hos ældre mennesker ikke er én tilstand, men mange, og ketamins effekt afhænger meget af hvilken type, du faktisk har. Det betyder noget, fordi det kan forklare, hvorfor nogle oplever drammatisk bedring, mens andre ser lille forandring, og det antyder, at vi skal blive meget bedre til at matche den rigtige behandling til den rigtige person. Studiet undersøgte, hvordan depression varierer blandt ældre patienter, og hvordan denne variation påvirker ketamins virkning. Når psykedelika-forskningen accelererer, peger dette fund på en afgørende grænse: at bevæge os fra en-løsning-for-alle-medicin mod præcisionsmedicin tilpasset individuel biologi og psykologi. At forstå disse forskelle er ikke blot akademisk—det er nøglen til at åbne psykedelikas rigtige potentiale i klinikken.

items.title: Low-dose lysergic acid diethylamide alters subjective visual perception but not visual contrast surround suppression.

summaries.en: Your eyes see things differently on LSD — colors pop, edges blur, the whole visual world feels more alive — yet a classic optical illusion stays stubbornly the same. That's the surprising finding from a new study where 30 people took low doses of LSD and reported vivid changes in how they perceived the world, but their brains' automatic visual trick (making contrasts look weaker when surrounded by bright patterns) didn't budge. Researchers used a careful, double-blind experiment to measure this, suggesting that the psychedelic's trippy visual effects come from a different part of how our brain processes the world than we thought. This adds an intriguing puzzle piece to our growing understanding of how psychedelics reshape perception — it turns out the magic isn't happening where scientists expected.
summaries.da: Dine øjne ser tingene anderledes på LSD — farver bliver lysere, kanter bliver slørere, hele den visuelle verden føles mere levende — og alligevel forbliver en klassisk optisk illusion stædig uændret. Det er det overraskende resultat fra et nyt studie, hvor 30 mennesker tog lave doser LSD og rapporterede levende ændringer i deres syn, men deres hjernes automatiske visuelle trick (at gøre kontraster se svagere ud når de er omgivet af lyse mønstre) rørte sig ikke. Forskerne brugte et omhyggeligt, dobbeltblindet eksperiment til at måle dette, hvilket tyder på at psykedelikaens trippy visuelle effekter kommer fra en anden del af hjernens visuelle behandling end videnskabsfolk forventede. Dette tilføjer et fascinerende puslespil til vores voksende forståelse af hvordan psykedelika omformer vores perception — det viser sig at magien ikke sker hvor forskere havde troet.

items.title: Methodological fragmentation and integration priorities in psychedelic-assisted therapy assessment: a scoping review.

summaries.en: Psychedelic-assisted therapy is showing real promise for treating depression, anxiety, and the existential struggles that come with serious illness—but here's the catch: researchers have been measuring results in wildly different ways, making it hard to know what actually works. A major new review looked at 59 studies to map out how scientists are evaluating everything from the initial screening through the psychedelic experience itself to the crucial integration work afterward, and they found both exciting progress and significant gaps. The good news? We now have solid tools for measuring the profound experiences people have, and clearer frameworks for training therapists. The bigger picture: psychedelic research is maturing fast, moving beyond just "does it work?" toward understanding exactly how to do it safely and effectively. Standardizing these methods matters enormously—it's the difference between promising findings and treatments that can actually reach people who need them.
summaries.da: Psykedelika-assisteret terapi viser virkelig potentiale for behandling af depression, angst og de eksistentielle kampe, der følger alvorlig sygdom—men her er hagen: forskere har målt resultaterne på voldsomt forskellige måder, hvilket gør det svært at vide, hvad der faktisk virker. En vigtig ny oversigt analyserede 59 studier for at kortlægge, hvordan videnskabsmænd evaluerer alt fra indledende screening gennem selve psykedelika-oplevelsen til det afgørende integrationsarbejde bagefter, og de fandt både spændende fremskridt og betydelige huller. Det gode: vi har nu solide værktøjer til at måle de dybe oplevelser, folk får, og klarere rammer for at træne terapeuter. Det større billede: psykedelika-forskningen modnes hurtigt og bevæger sig væk fra bare "virker det?" mod at forstå præcis hvordan man gør det sikkert og effektivt. At standardisere disse metoder betyder enormt meget—det er forskellen mellem lovende resultater og behandlinger, der faktisk kan nå mennesker, der har brug for dem.

items.title: A scoping review: ketamine or esketamine when used to assist psychotherapy or in combination with psychotherapy for the management of depression in adults.

summaries.en: What if the key to treating depression wasn't just the drug or just the therapy, but how they work together? A new review of 47 studies on ketamine and esketamine for depression reveals something intriguing: when combined with talk therapy, ketamine shows real promise—but we need to be honest about what we actually know. Right now, most evidence comes from small case studies and open trials, not the gold-standard controlled trials we'd want. Researchers looked at two main approaches: using ketamine during an altered state to enhance therapy (KAP), versus using it as a chemical support alongside regular therapy (KCP). Interestingly, while KAP captures most studies, the higher-quality research is starting to stack up around KCP—especially when paired with cognitive behavioral therapy. The bottom line? Psychedelics + therapy is a genuinely promising direction, but we're still in the early chapters. What this review makes crystal clear is that the next wave of research needs to be more rigorous, better documented, and honest about what's actually happening in the therapy room.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis løsningen på depression ikke bare var medicinen eller bare terapien, men hvordan de virker sammen? Et nyt review af 47 studier om ketamin og esketamin mod depression afslører noget fascinerende: når det kombineres med terapisamtaler, viser ketamin virkelig løfte—men vi skal være ærlige om, hvad vi faktisk ved. Lige nu kommer mest af beviserne fra små casestudier og åbne forsøg, ikke de guldstandard-kontrollerede studier, vi gerne ville have. Forskerne kiggede på to hovedtilgange: at bruge ketamin i en forandret bevidsthedstilstand for at styrke terapien, versus at bruge det som kemisk støtte ved siden af almindelig terapi. Interessant nok starter det højkvalitets-forskning at ophobe sig omkring den sidstnævnte tilgang—især når det kombineres med kognitiv adfærdsterapi. Pointen? Psykedelika + terapi er virkelig lovende, men vi er stadig i de tidlige kapitler. Det, som dette review gør krystalklart, er at den næste bølge af forskning skal være mere grundig, bedre dokumenteret og ærlig om, hvad der faktisk sker i terapirummet.

items.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context

summaries.en: Your brain on psychedelics doesn't retreat into itself—it actually becomes *more* responsive to what's happening around you. A massive new study tracking 62 people's brains during psilocybin use found something surprising: their neural activity synced up remarkably well with their actual environment, whether they were listening to music, watching a film, or meditating. People whose brains showed this kind of context-awareness were the same ones reporting profoundly meaningful experiences. Researchers used advanced brain imaging and machine learning to map how psilocybin reorganizes neural networks—revealing patterns that standard analysis had missed. This finding reframes how we think about psychedelics: rather than fragmenting consciousness, they seem to create a more unified brain state that's exquisitely attuned to the present moment. As psychedelic science moves toward therapeutic applications, understanding this context-sensitivity could be key to optimizing how we use these compounds to help people heal.
summaries.da: Dit hjerne på psykedelika trækker sig ikke ind i sig selv—den bliver faktisk *mere* responsiv over for det, der sker omkring dig. Et massivt nyt studie af 62 menneskers hjerner under psilocybin-brug fandt noget overraskende: deres neural aktivitet synkroniserede sig bemærkelsesværdigt godt med deres faktiske miljø, uanset om de lyttede til musik, så en film eller mediterede. De mennesker, hvis hjerner viste denne kontekst-bevidsthed, var præcis dem, der rapporterede dybt meningsfulde oplevelser. Forskere brugte avanceret hjerneafbildning og maskinlæring til at kortlægge, hvordan psilocybin reorganiserer neurale netværk—og afslørede mønstre, som standardanalyse havde overset. Dette fund omfortolker, hvordan vi tænker om psykedelika: i stedet for at fragmentere bevidstheden ser de ud til at skabe en mere samlet hjernestatus, der er ekstraordinært tilpasset det øjeblik, vi lever i. Efterhånden som psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig mod terapeutiske anvendelser, kunne forståelsen af denne kontekst-følsomhed blive afgørende for at optimere, hvordan vi bruger disse stoffer til at hjælpe mennesker med at hele.

items.title: Interoceptive effects of N

summaries.en: New psychedelics are popping up on the gray market, and scientists just discovered something crucial: tiny chemical tweaks to LSD's structure can dramatically change how your body *feels* the drug — affecting everything from heart rate to body temperature awareness. Researchers tested these novel compounds and found that small molecular changes create wildly different experiences, even when the trip itself might look similar. This lab study examined how these altered molecules interact with your body's sensing systems using cellular tests. It's a crucial piece of the puzzle as psychedelic research moves beyond asking "does it work?" to understanding *how* and *why* — knowledge that could help scientists design safer, more predictable treatments while also showing why unregulated versions are genuinely unpredictable.
summaries.da: Nye psykedelika dukker op på gråmarkedet, og forskere har lige opdaget noget afgørende: små kemiske ændringer af LSD's struktur kan dramatisk ændre, hvordan din krop *mærker* stoffet — og påvirker alt fra puls til kropstemperaturbevidsthed. Forskerne testede disse nye forbindelser og fandt, at små molekylære justeringer skaber vidt forskellige oplevelser, selvom trippen selv kan ligne hinanden. Studiet undersøgte, hvordan de ændrede molekyler interagerer med kroppens sensorsystemer ved hjælp af cellulære tests. Det er et afgørende puslespil-stykke, mens psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig fra at spørge "virker det?" til at forstå *hvordan* og *hvorfor* — viden, der kunne hjælpe forskere med at designe sikrere, mere forudsigelige behandlinger og samtidig vise, hvorfor uregulerede versioner er uforudsigeligt farlige.

items.title: From network destabilisation to adaptive reconfiguration: A hippocampal longitudinal Axis model of psychedelic therapy.

summaries.en: Your brain on psychedelics might be doing something counterintuitive: it gets messier before it gets better. New research suggests that psychedelics temporarily shake up the balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain—essentially loosening rigid patterns of thinking that keep people stuck in anxiety, depression, or trauma. But here's the hopeful part: this destabilisation isn't the whole story. What follows is a rebuilding phase where the brain rewires itself in healthier ways, and those changes stick around even after the drug wears off. Scientists looked at how the hippocampus (your memory and emotion hub) might coordinate this two-phase process across different brain regions. This framework helps explain why one psychedelic session can catalyse months of lasting improvement—and why different people might benefit in different ways. As psychedelic therapy moves from fringe to mainstream medicine, understanding exactly how these shifts happen at the brain level is crucial for making treatments safer, more targeted, and available to more people who need them.
summaries.da: Dit hjerne på psykedelika gør måske noget kontraintuitivt: det bliver rodet før det bliver bedre. Ny forskning tyder på, at psykedelika midlertidigt ryster balancen mellem excitation og inhibition i hjernen—det vil sige løsner stive tankeomønstre, der holder mennesker fast i angst, depression eller traumer. Men det glædelige er: denne destabilisering er ikke hele historien. Det, der følger, er en genopbygningsfase, hvor hjernen rekonstruerer sig selv på sundere måder, og disse forandringer bliver ved selv efter stoffet forsvinder. Forskere undersøgte, hvordan hippocampus (dit hukommelses- og følelsescenter) måske koordinerer denne tofasede proces på tværs af forskellige hjernebereolmder. Denne rammeværk hjælper med at forklare, hvorfor en enkelt psykedelika-session kan katalysere måneder med varig forbedring—og hvorfor forskellige mennesker måske får gavn på forskellige måder. Når psykedelika-terapi bevæger sig fra periferi til mainstream-medicin, er det afgørende at forstå præcist, hvordan disse skift sker på hjernelevel, for at gøre behandlingen sikrere, mere målrettet og tilgængelig for flere mennesker, der har brug for det.

items.title: Suicidal ideation covaries with depressive severity during six-month real-world esketamine treatment in a cohort enriched for borderline personality disorder.

summaries.en: When people with severe depression and borderline personality disorder received esketamine treatment over six months, their suicidal thoughts dropped alongside their overall depression — suggesting that rapid-acting treatments might offer real hope for those in crisis. Researchers tracked real patients in actual clinical settings, watching how their symptoms changed over time, and the results point to something important: as depression lifted, so did the dangerous ideation that often comes with it. This fits into a crucial shift happening right now in psychiatry — moving beyond traditional antidepressants to explore how compounds like esketamine work differently, offering faster relief when people need it most. It's early evidence that these tools might help rewire how we respond to severe mental health emergencies.
summaries.da: Da mennesker med svær depression og borderline personlighedsforstyrrelser fik esketaminbehandling over seks måneder, faldt deres selvmordstanker sammen med deres generelle depression — hvilket tyder på, at hurtigtvirkende behandlinger kan give håb til dem, der er i krise. Forskerne fulgte virkelige patienter i dagligdags kliniske omgivelser og så, hvordan deres symptomer ændrede sig over tid, og resultaterne peger på noget vigtigt: når depressionen lettede, gjorde selvmordstankerne det også. Det passer ind i et afgørende skift, der sker nu inden for psykiatrien — væk fra traditionelle antidepressiva og hen mod at udforske, hvordan psykedelika som esketamin fungerer anderledes og tilbyder hurtigere lindring, når mennesker har brug for det mest. Det er tidlig evidens for, at disse værktøjer kan hjælpe os med at genskabe vores reaktion på alvorlige psykiske sundhedskriser.

items.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context.

summaries.en: Your brain normally divides itself into isolated networks — one for daydreaming, another for focused tasks, another for sensing the world around you. New research shows that psychedelics essentially break down these walls, allowing your brain's different regions to communicate and sync up in ways they usually don't. The result? A brain that's more unified, more responsive to what's actually happening in the moment. Scientists measured brain activity patterns in people under the influence and found this increased alignment between internal and external awareness — which might explain why psychedelics can feel so vivid and present. This study adds a crucial piece to our growing understanding of how psychedelics reshape consciousness at the neurological level, moving us beyond 'what does it feel like?' toward 'here's what's actually happening in your brain.' As research continues to map these changes, we're getting closer to understanding not just the experience itself, but the mechanisms that could make psychedelics valuable tools for healing.
summaries.da: Dit hjerne organiserer sig normalt i isolerede netværk — et til dagdrømme, et til fokuserede opgaver, et til at sanser verden omkring dig. Ny forskning viser, at psykedelika essensen bryder ned disse mure og lader dine hjernes forskellige områder kommunikere og synkronisere på måder, de normalt ikke gør. Resultatet? En hjerne, der er mere samlet, mere responsiv overfor det, der faktisk sker i øjeblikket. Forskere målte hjernens aktivitetsmønstre hos mennesker under påvirkning og fandt denne øgede tilpasning mellem indre og ydre bevidsthed — hvilket kunne forklare, hvorfor psykedelika føles så levende og tilstedeværende. Dette studie tilføjer et afgørende stykke til vores voksende forståelse af, hvordan psykedelika omformer bevidstheden på neurologisk niveau, og bevæger os væk fra 'hvordan føles det?' mod 'her er hvad der faktisk sker i din hjerne.' Når forskningen fortsætter med at kortlægge disse ændringer, kommer vi tættere på at forstå ikke blot oplevelsen selv, men de mekanismer, der kunne gøre psykedelika til værdifulde værktøjer for healing.

items.title: Credentials, Clinics, and Costs: Stakeholders Respond to HRSA’s Psychedelic Therapy RFI

summaries.en: The U.S. government is seriously asking: how do we actually make psychedelic therapy work in real clinics? The Health Resources and Services Administration just collected nearly 60 expert responses on everything from therapist training to cost and clinic setup—and the answers reveal just how close we are to seeing psilocybin and MDMA treatments move from research labs into everyday medical practice. This matters because it's not just about whether these drugs work (they do, according to recent trials)—it's about building the infrastructure so regular people can actually access them. Researchers, therapists, and healthcare leaders are weighing in on what credentials therapists need, how to train them, and what this costs, painting a picture of what psychedelic-assisted therapy could look like when it becomes standard medicine. This is the blueprint phase, the moment where science meets real-world logistics.
summaries.da: Den amerikanske regering stiller det store spørgsmål: hvordan gør vi psykedelika-terapi til virkelighed i almindelige klinikker? Health Resources and Services Administration har netop samlet tæt på 60 ekspertsvar om alt fra terapeutuddannelse til omkostninger og klinikopbygning—og svarene viser, hvor tæt vi er på at få psilocybin- og MDMA-behandlinger fra forskningsmiljøer ind i daglig praksis. Det betyder noget, fordi det ikke bare handler om, hvorvidt disse stoffer virker (det gør de, ifølge seneste studier)—det handler om at bygge infrastrukturen, så almindelige mennesker faktisk kan få adgang til dem. Forskere, terapeuter og sundhedsledere vejer ind på, hvilke kvalifikationer terapeuter skal have, hvordan man uddanner dem, og hvad det koster, og tegner et billede af, hvad psykedelika-assisteret terapi kunne ligne, når det bliver standardmedicin. Det er skitseringsfasen, det øjeblik hvor videnskab møder virkelighed.

items.title: Ketamine's impact on rumination-related brain dynamics: insights from a randomized controlled fMRI trial.

summaries.en: Your brain gets stuck in loops when you're ruminating—literally. A new brain imaging study found that ketamine quickly quiets a specific brain pattern linked to anxious, repetitive thinking, especially in people who ruminate most. The effect was temporary, fading within 24 hours, but it offers a concrete window into how this psychedelic might interrupt the brain dynamics that keep depression going. Researchers gave 75 healthy people either ketamine or a placebo, scanning their brains before, during, and after treatment to map which networks activated together. This fits perfectly into growing evidence that psychedelics work differently than traditional antidepressants—they don't just boost chemicals, they reshape how brain regions talk to each other, potentially breaking unhelpful patterns at their source.
summaries.da: Din hjerne skal blive fanget i løkker, når du grubler—helt bogstaveligt. Et nyt hjernescanning-studie viste, at ketamin hurtigt dæmper et specifikt hjernmønster forbundet med angstfyldt, gentagen tænkning, især hos mennesker der grubler mest. Effekten var kortvarig og forsvandt inden for 24 timer, men den giver et konkret indblik i, hvordan denne psykedelika kan afbryde de hjernedynamikker, der holder depression på plads. Forskerne gav 75 raske mennesker enten ketamin eller placebo og scannede deres hjerner før, under og efter behandlingen for at kortlægge, hvilke netværk der blev aktiveret sammen. Det passer perfekt ind i stigende evidens for, at psykedelika fungerer anderledes end traditionelle antidepressiva—de øger ikke bare kemikalier, de omformer, hvordan hjernedele taler sammen, og kan potentielt bryde uønskede mønstre ved deres kilde.

items.title: The Timing of Plasticity: Beyond Synapses in Psychedelic Therapeutics.

summaries.en:
Here's something that might shift how we think about psychedelics: they don't just rewire your brain in the moment — they seem to open a window of opportunity for deeper changes to stick around. New research is zooming in on the timing of how psychedelics create plasticity — that crucial ability of the brain to form new connections and break old patterns. This isn't just academic; it means the real therapeutic magic might happen in the days and weeks after a psychedelic experience, when your brain is primed to learn and change in ways that weren't possible before.

Scientists are moving beyond the old story of just looking at synapses (the connections between brain cells) to understand the fuller picture of how psychedelics create lasting shifts. This research sits right at the heart of where modern psychedelic science is heading: from "what happens during the trip?" to "how do we harness these windows of plasticity to build real, lasting healing?" It's the kind of insight that could eventually help therapists and researchers design better protocols and know exactly when therapeutic work lands hardest.
summaries.da:
Her er noget, der måske ændrer på, hvordan vi tænker om psykedelika: de rewirer ikke bare din hjerne i øjeblikket — de ser ud til at åbne et mulighedsvindue for dybere forandringer, der kan blive ved. Ny forskning zoomer ind på timingen af, hvordan psykedelika skaber plastisitet — den afgørende evne hos hjernen til at danne nye forbindelser og bryde gamle mønstre. Det er ikke bare akademisk; det betyder, at den rigtige terapeutiske magi måske sker i dagene og ugerne efter en psykedelisk oplevelse, når din hjerne er parat til at lære og ændre sig på måder, der før var umulige.

Forskere bevæger sig væk fra den gamle historie om bare at kigge på synapser (forbindelserne mellem hjerneceller) hen imod at forstå det større billede af, hvordan psykedelika skaber varige skift. Denne forskning sidder midt i kernen af, hvor moderne psykedelisk videnskab er på vej: fra "hvad sker der under turen?" til "hvordan udnytter vi disse plasticitetsvinduer til at bygge ægte, varig helbredelse?" Det er netop den slags indsigt, der kan hjælpe terapeuter og forskere med at designe bedre protokoller.

items.title: The Sacred Dimension: Psychedelic Use and Motivations for Use Predict Religiosity and Spiritual Practices

summaries.en: People who use psychedelics often report deeper spiritual experiences—and a new study suggests this isn't just coincidence. Researchers found that psychedelic use actually predicts increased religiosity and spiritual practices, meaning these experiences genuinely reshape how people relate to meaning, transcendence, and their place in the world. This matters because it challenges the idea that psychedelics are purely recreational: for many users, they're catalysts for profound existential reflection. The study examined how motivations for use and actual psychedelic experiences correlate with spiritual development. As psychedelic research moves from the lab into real-world contexts, understanding these spiritual dimensions becomes crucial—not because we need to prove psychedelics are 'spiritual,' but because recognizing this connection helps us appreciate the full spectrum of how these medicines affect human consciousness and wellbeing.
summaries.da: Folk der bruger psykedelika rapporterer ofte dybere åndelige erfaringer—og et nyt studie antyder, at det ikke bare er tilfælde. Forskere fandt, at psykedelika-brug faktisk forudsiger øget religiøsitet og åndelige praksisser, hvilket betyder, at disse oplevelser virkelig omformer, hvordan mennesker forholder sig til betydning, transcendens og deres plads i verden. Det vigtige er, at det udfordrer ideen om, at psykedelika blot er rekreativt: for mange brugere er de katalysatorer for dyb eksistentiel refleksion. Studiet undersøgte, hvordan motivationer for brug og faktiske psykedelika-erfaringer korrelerer med åndelig udvikling. Når psykedelika-forskning bevæger sig fra laboratoriet ind i virkelige kontekster, bliver forståelsen af disse åndelige dimensioner afgørende—ikke fordi vi skal bevise, at psykedelika er 'åndelige,' men fordi denne indsigt hjælper os med at værdsætte det fulde spektrum af, hvordan disse lægemidler påvirker menneskelig bevidsthed og trivsel.

items.title: The Abuse Liability of Classic Psychedelics: A Methodological Critique and Assessment of the Quality of Evidence of Recent Studies

summaries.en:
Good news: research suggests classic psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD have surprisingly low abuse potential compared to other drugs. But here's the catch—we need to be careful about celebrating too loudly.
